sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ultimate purpose of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is for the revelation to be from the perspective of the lower world itself, like a field that is worked.

translations.translation: And one must add in explanation of the verse's wording "to a worked field,"
for the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is that the G-dly revelation drawn into the lower worlds will be from the aspect of the lower worlds themselves.
And it can be said,
that this is the reason that the revelation through the mitzvos is through the place where the mitzvah is performed being prepared for the revelation
[and as mentioned above
(section 2)
that the Garden of Eden is called a field because the Garden of Eden is a place prepared for the revelation through the sowing of mitzvos.
And likewise regarding the place of the entire world,
that "He sent him... to work the ground" is to make the place of the world prepared for the revelation through the mitzvos],
because through the drawing of revelation into the world through the mitzvah being also according to the
(place of the)
world being prepared for this,
the revelation in the world is from the aspect of the world itself.
And this is "a king to a worked field,"
for the completeness of the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is that the revelation in the world will be
(not only from the aspect of the fulfillment of the mitzvah,
but also)
from the aspect of the world,
the field,
and since this that there becomes, so to speak, the aspect of the essence of the light,
the Supernal King,
is for the sake of this intention,
therefore "a king to a worked field."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that man was expelled from Eden to make the lowest world a dwelling place for Him from its own aspect, paralleling the revelation from the field to the earth.

translations.translation: And to add,
that the reason
(in the inwardness of the matters)
for man being banished from the Garden of Eden is,
because the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is that the dwelling will be in the lowest, of which there is no lower below it,
and that the dwelling in it will be from its aspect
(of this lowest),
and therefore "Hashem Elokim sent him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground,"
to make the place of the world
(the most lowest)
prepared for the revelation,
so that even the lowest, of which there is no lower below it, will be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
and that the dwelling in it will be from its aspect.
And likewise regarding the matter of field and earth above,
that the ultimate intention in the drawing of the revelation of the aspect of the Supernal King into the field,
the inwardness of Malchus,
is,
that through this the revelation will be drawn into the earth,
the externality of Malchus
(and through this into Biyah,
until this lowest physical world),
and in a manner that the revelation in the earth will be
(not like something additional upon it,
but rather this)
will be the very essence of the earth,
similar to the inwardness of Malchus
(the field)
whose essence is that it receives the revelations that are above it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the order of Sarah's years hints that the revelation of the Supernal King was drawn also into the aspect of "all" and then into the lower worlds.

translations.translation: And this is "And the lives of Sarah were one hundred years and twenty years and seven years,"
and it is explained in the maamar,
that "one hundred years" is the inwardness of Kesser,
the aspect of the Supernal King.
"Twenty years and seven years" are the mochin and midos
(that are drawn through the Yesod),
the aspect of "all."
And explanation is needed,
behold, that Sarah merited supernal life was in a manner of from below upward,
first the aspect of "all" and afterwards the aspect of the Supernal King,
but the order in the verse is "one hundred years" and afterwards "twenty years and seven years."
And one can say the explanation,
that it is in order to hint that the drawing of the aspect of "one hundred years,"
the Supernal King,
was drawn afterwards also into the aspect of "twenty years and seven years,"
the aspect of "all."
And through this,
the revelation of the aspect of "one hundred years" that was drawn first into the aspect of field
(the inwardness of Malchus)
was drawn afterwards also into the aspect of earth
(the externality of Malchus).
And afterwards it says "the years of the life of Sarah,"
that she drew this revelation also into Biyah.
